title: Ignorance preserves order; the comedy of masks; why corruption hurts; harmony as the ordering causes great good
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): From these results ye harmonic goodness that same stands as ye end belonging toward things. For all things come by means belonging toward necessity toward ye sake belonging toward fate plus harmony. that same which we call HARMONY, founded in ye being plus order belonging toward things, that same stands as in necessity plus fate — since therefore all corruptions plus generations belonging toward things plus actions stand as not toward ye sake belonging toward ye things alone — because they themselves stand as driven by means belonging toward pain plus pleasure toward others ends — it follows that same ye ordering cause draws out from such order a great plus divine good. second, that same while dying they may resist ye causes bringing death plus modify them toward fates uses. first, lest other living things also wish to die before their time; — it stands as answered. why do things grieve when they stand as corrupted, plus as it were resist death? But you say: as toward playing Its play plus comedy — that they exist toward so long as has been decreed by means belonging toward ye divine power. And this stands as fate: plus grieves among things that same destroy it — for a human being rejoices to be among things that same conserve his nature. God gave them pain plus pleasure — but that same things may be kept in ye life they stand as allotted. and coercion stands as truly such when things stand as driven against their propensity plus against ye love added to them. Affections plus actions stand as brought forth out from coercion plus love together; And truly, whoever lifts himself to ye Author belonging toward things plus with Him looks upon this as a comedy in that same which all things stand as masked by means belonging toward certain larvas — some appearing good plus beautiful, others evil plus deformed — sees that same when ye masks stand as laid aside they agree beautifully. Therefore, since all things stand as good plus safe, it stands as best toward ye worlds order that same some things appear to others evil plus foul, lest they fall back into chaos. they would do nothing against one another, nor preserve their own life, plus all would turn into chaos — for if each thing knew that same all other things stand as beautiful. But eternal wisdom uses our ignorance toward our life.
pass_b_english: But eternal wisdom uses our ignorance for our life. For if each thing knew that all other things are beautiful, they would do nothing against one another, nor preserve their own life, and all would turn into chaos. Therefore, since all things are good and safe, it is best for the worlds order that some things appear to others evil and foul, lest they fall back into chaos. And truly, whoever lifts himself to the Author of things and with Him looks upon this as a comedy in which all things are masked by certain larvas — some appearing good and beautiful, others evil and deformed — sees that when the masks are laid aside they agree beautifully.

Affections and actions are brought forth from coercion and love together; and coercion is truly such when things are driven against their propensity and against the love added to them. But that things may be kept in the life they are allotted, God gave them pain and pleasure. For a human being rejoices to be among things that conserve his nature, and grieves among things that destroy it. And this is fate: that they exist for so long as has been decreed by the divine power, as for playing Its play and comedy.

But you say: why do things grieve when they are corrupted, and as it were resist death? It is answered, first, lest other living things also wish to die before their time; second, that while dying they may resist the causes bringing death and modify them for fates uses. Since therefore all corruptions and generations of things and actions are not for the sake of the things alone — because they themselves are driven by pain and pleasure toward others ends — it follows that the ordering cause draws from such order a great and divine good, which we call HARMONY, founded in the being and order of things, that is in necessity and fate. For all things come by necessity for the sake of fate and harmony. From these results the harmonic goodness that is the end of things.
source_text: Sapientia vero aeterna utitur nostra ignorantia ad vitam nostram. Si enim singulae res scirent omnes alias res esse pulchras, utique nihil agerent contra invicem, nec propriam servarent vitam, omnia in chaos converterentur. Quapropter cum omnia sint bona et tuta, optimum est ad mundi ordinem ut videantur aliae res aliis malae et turpes, ne recidant in chaos. Et sane, qui ad authorem rerum se elevat et cum eo inspicit hanc quasi comoediam, in qua res omnes quibusdam personantur larvis, aliae apparent bonae et pulchrae, aliae malae et deformes, videt depositis larvis pulchre convenire. Affectiones et actiones a coactione et amore simul eduntur, et tunc vera est coactio, quando contra propensionem et amorem additum res aguntur. Sed ut serventur res in vita quam sortiuntur, dedit illis Deus dolorem et voluptatem. Gaudet enim homo esse in conservativis suae naturae, et dolet in destructivis. Et hoc est fatum, ut tanto tempore sint ut divino numini, quasi ad ludum et comoediam suam agendam, decretum est. Sed dicis: quare dum corrumpuntur res dolent, mortique quasi repugnant? Respondetur primo hoc fieri ne et caetera viventía ante suum tempus vellent mori. Secundo, ut dum moriuntur, repugnent causis afferentibus mortem ac modificent illas ad fati utilitates. Cum ergo omnes corruptiones et generationes rerum et actiones non sint propter ipsas res modo, quoniam ipsae dolore et voluptate aguntur ad fines aliorum, consequens est ut causa ordinatrix eliciat e talium ordine magnum divinumque bonum, quod vocamus HARMONIAM, quae fundatur in rerum esse et ordine, hoc est necessitate et fato. Omnia enim necessitate veniunt propter fatum et harmoniam. Ex his vero resultat harmonica bonitas, quae est finis rerum.
